clue.text: Club field unevenly spoilt

parts.note: a spoon is an old golf club, a lofted wooden one

indicators.note: unevenly says take the odd-numbered letters, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A golf club is said to have been ruined by a bumpy, uneven course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unevenly' keeps the letters in odd positions of 'field', giving FED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pampered and given everything without effort is described as having had it all handed to them, an idiom for being spoilt.

clue.text: Capital chap!

parts.note: reads like an old-fashioned compliment, 'splendid fellow!', but means a man from a capital city, here France's

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned exclamation of praise for a splendid fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' as praise is the misdirection; read it as a capital city, and the chap is a man from Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A native or resident of Paris, the French capital, is a man from a capital city.

clue.text: Ground almonds carry a touch of dill plant

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' rearranges ALMONDS into OLDMANS; then BEAR and D, the first letter of 'dill'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the common name of wild clematis, a climbing plant with fluffy grey seed heads.

clue.text: It's essential to waterproof a bricklaying material

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: Sum up year as time of critical action

explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ADD into DDA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The term, from the 1944 Normandy landings, now means any day on which a critical operation begins.

clue.text: Sceptic a good Catholic's entertaining is not after conversion

explanation.walkthrough: 'after conversion' rearranges IS NOT into NOSTI, which 'entertaining' puts between AG and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds that God's existence cannot be known is a religious doubter, a kind of sceptic.

clue.text: Voice disapproval over posh short skirt

explanation.surface: Someone clicks their tongue at a posh person's skimpy skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina's skirt is short and stiff, made of layered net.

clue.text: Ambassador's notice announced force in support

explanation.walkthrough: WREST and REST sound the same, so 'announced' gives REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushioned rest on a seat back holds the head up, so it is a support.

clue.text: Scoundrel and weed touring America in this — that's out of favour

explanation.surface: A rogue goes round America weeding, and has fallen into disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads with the answer: someone 'in the doghouse' is out of favour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in the doghouse' describes someone in disgrace, so this is the place a disgraced person is said to be.

clue.text: Government's free network

parts.note: G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.definitionFit: A person aged between eighty and eighty-nine, as Elizabeth II then was, is described by this word.

clue.text: Parking in front of pub, have drink around Canadian capital's highest point

clue.text: Heavens above! There's no beginning to restraint

clue.text: Up north veg is cheap reportedly

explanation.definitionFit: This is the Scots and northern English word for a potato, a vegetable.

clue.text: Handle king and jack

clue.text: It acts as a reminder to store alcoholic drink

clue.text: Mathematician's sign for peers
